title: Revealment bounded by average cost
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $Omega$ be a finite input alphabet, and let $T$ be a randomized decision tree on $n$ coordinates with a finite nonempty seed space and a probability law on its seeds, such that every seed selects a tree computing the same function. For any probability distribution $pi$ on $Omega$, the largest, over coordinates, of the probability that the tree queries that coordinate on an independent product-distributed input is at most the expected number of queries under that input distribution.
